A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, research questions, benchmarks, and interventions. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained figures and tables can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, reasoning-budget experiments, extraction attacks, RANA interventions, and a manual leakage annotation study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds Phi-4 and closed-model evaluations, statistical tests, and an evaluator comparison.

M1.justification: RANA and budget forcing remain unchanged. V2 adds a limited closed-model adaptation of the extraction attack, with additional reasoning-start cues in Appendix E, Extraction Prompt 2. The existing open-model attacks are principally documented more fully.

E1.justification: Both versions use AirGapAgent-R with the same synthetic profiles, fields, and scenarios, and AgentDAM with the same three domains. AirGapAgent-R-small names a retained benchmark subset; additional models and evaluator checks do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated comparison set: Table 3 adds vanilla, CoT, and reasoning variants from the Phi-4-mini and Phi-4 families; Table 5 adds o4-mini and claude-4-sonnet. Appendix C also directly compares the existing gpt-4o-mini evaluator with gpt-4o.

E3.justification: The reported budget-forcing subset changes from 640 to 624 prompts, without establishing a rerun. Added experiments evaluate available reasoning summaries from closed models and compare evaluators on 100 sampled traces. Appendix A.2 inconsistently says 642 prompts, leaving the exact closed-model sample count unclear.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a manual comparison of two evaluators' extractions on 100 reasoning traces. Appendix A.2 extends the injection analysis to two closed models. The existing budget sensitivity, RANA, swapping intervention, and 200-item leakage annotation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds one-sided McNemar tests, exact binomial tests against a 0.1% null threshold, and Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment, with significance annotations in figures and tables. This substantially extends v1's statistical reporting. The existing seed information is retained; additional repeated runs are not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for the Phi families and closed models, plus the finding that gpt-4o-mini extracts the same or more sensitive data than gpt-4o in 93/100 cases. Table 5 reports o4-mini answer privacy of 76.1% without injection and 73.2% with injection. A retained entry also changes: DeepSeek-R1 AgentDAM privacy is 0.94 in v1 Table 3 versus 91.4% in v2 Table 4. Most other retained scores differ only in displayed precision.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. V2 expresses the existing utility and privacy metrics as probabilities and task-count ratios; this is explanatory formalization rather than a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about reasoning leakage, extraction risks, and utility–privacy trade-offs. The conclusion's model count increases from 13 to 17, reflecting expanded supporting evidence rather than a redefined contribution.

C2.justification: V2 revises the open-model-only limitation and discusses leakage in summarized reasoning. Table 5 explicitly warns that closed-model trace privacy is not directly comparable with other models, including because OpenAI returns approximately 8% of traces. Appendix A.2 adds a speculative explanation involving internal filtering of missing summaries.

D1.justification: Appendix E supplies exact extraction prompts absent from v1's appendix. V2 also adds Phi checkpoints and generation parameters, identifies the small subset used for Figure 5, and explains task-success checking. Existing hardware disclosures, code links, and dataset links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the two Phi reasoning reports, Benjamini–Hochberg, and Wu et al. (2025b). It explicitly positions Wu et al. as parallel research reaching similar conclusions about scaling and trace extraction through adversarial attacks. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 expands metric explanations, adds statistical-testing prose and a closed-model appendix subsection, and makes localized wording and cross-reference edits. The main narrative and section sequence are retained; the existing appendix analyses are renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: The combined benchmark table becomes separate probing and agentic tables, and a closed-model table is added. Figure 2 gains Phi points and expanded axes; Figures 4–5 gain significance markers. New extraction-prompt boxes and relocated displays retain the established visual style.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and evidential support through explicit attack prompts, statistical testing, an evaluator cross-check, and additional model comparisons with stated comparability limits. These are useful but bounded gains. Reporting inconsistencies remain, including 624 versus 642 prompts and the changed DeepSeek-R1 AgentDAM table entry without a corresponding Figure 2 update.
